title: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and check what it can read
summary: Start with one pretend note so you can tell where each answer came from.

intro.what: Microsoft 365 Copilot is a helper for work apps. Your account, license and permissions determine which tools and files you can use.
intro.features: Copilot Chat can work from a prompt or an uploaded file. Some accounts also have Work IQ, which can draw on work content the signed-in person may read.
intro.exchange: Check whether Copilot can read the approved training notice you intended.
intro.m365: Identify the account and linked document behind a draft.
intro.developer: Compare an answer grounded in an attached spec with one given without it.

sections.title: Find the source
paragraphs: Sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the account you mean to use. Create a pretend note: “The early shift moves to 8 a.m. on May 6.” Give Copilot just this note. Ask which shift changes, what time it starts and who owns the change. Open its source. The note gives no owner. With Work IQ enabled, you can also ask about work files you already have permission to read.
A reply may draw from mail, a Teams conversation or a file your work account can read. Open its source to check both the words and which account had access.

sections.title: Try more thinking where it helps
paragraphs: Where available, the chat menu offers Auto, Quick response and Think deeper. Try Quick response to make the note shorter. Add an older draft that says May 5 and ask it to compare both. Check which note was approved before deciding which date belongs in a reminder. A longer answer still needs a source for its date.
sources: Microsoft · grounding and the Work IQ control

title: Find what was really decided
summary: Separate an offer, a request and a firm promise in a mail thread or a meeting.

intro.what: Copilot in Outlook can sum up a thread of messages. Copilot in Teams can help you follow a meeting when the settings allow it.
intro.features: Mail summaries can link back to messages. A meeting summary may use a saved transcript or meeting chat. Check the material each one could read.
intro.exchange: Separate a proposed mail restart from an approved restart in meeting notes.
intro.m365: Find the transcript line that assigns an action to its owner.
intro.developer: Turn a feature discussion into decided changes and open questions.
sources: Microsoft · summarizing an email thread in Outlook
Microsoft · meeting modes, transcript coverage and recap

sections.title: Read the last real answer in Outlook
paragraphs: Open a practice thread or paste these three lines into Copilot Chat. “We can deliver Tuesday.” “Can you do Wednesday?” “We will check.” Ask what time is confirmed and what still needs a reply. Wednesday is a request. Read the last line yourself. A useful draft asks for confirmation. Review names, dates and recipients before sending a real message.
sources: Microsoft · summarizing an email thread in Outlook
Microsoft · what Copilot Chat can use inside each app

sections.title: Check which meeting words are saved
paragraphs: In Teams, the organizer and the meeting rules affect what Copilot can use. A during-meeting setting can use speech without saving a transcript for later. For a past decision, see whether a transcript or a written chat exists.

Try the source line “Maybe Friday. We need to ask the reviewer.” Ask for the decision, owner and due date. Friday is only a suggestion. The line gives no firm owner. Check each claimed decision against the saved words.
sources: Microsoft · meeting modes, transcript coverage and recap

title: Turn a checked note into four slides
summary: Build a short slide deck where every title matches the numbers.

intro.what: Copilot can help write a note in Word and use an approved file to draft a presentation in PowerPoint.
intro.features: Ask for a short brief with headings. Build slides from the brief. Label each chart so readers know who was counted.
intro.exchange: Use a checked service note as the sole source for a mail update slide.
intro.m365: Trace each claim in a four-slide deck back to the original document.
intro.developer: Keep the known test result distinct from the planned release in your demo.
sources: Microsoft · working from an existing document in Word
Microsoft · making a presentation from a Word brief

sections.title: Write the note in Word
paragraphs: Use this practice data: 12 teams were invited. Nine replied. Six of those nine would continue. Ask for three headings: Invitation, Replies and Decision. Read the counts. Six of nine who replied favored continuing. Six out of all twelve is half. Missing replies give no vote either way. Save the corrected note.
sources: Microsoft · working from an existing document in Word

sections.title: Make and check the slides
paragraphs: Open PowerPoint, choose Copilot where available and give it your approved Word file. Request a title slide, a participation slide, a results slide and a next-step slide. A chart about replies needs a label saying “9 replies.” If it says most invited teams voted yes, revise it. Exactly half of those invited gave a yes response.
sources: Microsoft · making a presentation from a Word brief

title: Check the numbers in Excel
summary: Change one cell and see whether the result changes with it.

intro.what: Excel stores related values in rows and columns. Copilot can suggest formulas or help you work with a table in a supported workbook.
intro.features: A formula tells the sheet how to calculate. You can inspect the cells it uses and try one change to see if the answer updates.
intro.exchange: Add counts of shared mailboxes while keeping zero-count rows.
intro.m365: Inspect the Excel formula after another team adds a row.
intro.developer: Use a tiny score sheet to test totals before coding your scoreboard.
sources: Microsoft · editing, supported settings and recovery in Excel
Microsoft · what Copilot Chat can use inside each app

sections.title: Make a small table
paragraphs: A packing team wants to know how many items it can ship. The sheet records the packed and rejected items separately for each batch.

Make a new practice workbook. Enter these rows as numbers. Turn the range into a table named Shipments. Ask for an Accepted column equal to Packed minus Rejected. If your account gives instructions in chat, enter the formula there in your practice sheet.
sources: Microsoft · editing, supported settings and recovery in Excel

sections.title: Change one cell
paragraphs: Accepted should show 114, 54, 12 and 0. Together, 180 out of 200 were accepted, or 90%. The formula is =SUM(Shipments[Accepted])/SUM(Shipments[Packed]). For a table with no packed units, choose a clear result such as “No units packed.”
Change B’s rejected number from 6 to 9. Now you should have 177 out of 200, or 88.5%. If the total stays at 180, click the total cell. Is it a fixed number or a formula that reads the updated rows?
sources: Microsoft · editing, supported settings and recovery in Excel

title: Choose a coding helper or a handbook helper
summary: Pick the tool by the job the next person needs done.

intro.what: GitHub Copilot helps with code. Agent Builder makes a helper for repeated questions. Copilot Studio can connect a helper to tools and actions.
intro.features: A coding helper can propose an edit. A handbook helper can answer from a given file. A service action can make a real record after someone asks for it.
intro.exchange: Choose a handbook helper for policy questions about a practice mailbox.
intro.m365: Ask a handbook agent to point to the clause behind a file-sharing answer.
intro.developer: Choose a coding agent when the job needs a change to a project file.
sources: GitHub · choosing an agent and working environment
Microsoft · Agent Builder and Copilot Studio compared

sections.title: Fix a file with GitHub Copilot
paragraphs: Open a practice project in a supported editor or give its connected coding agent a task. Ask it to export and reimport one field named “Deck A, Row 2.” A comma usually starts the next box in a CSV file. The field here must stay in one box. Open the exported file again and check that it gives the exact original words.
sources: GitHub · choosing an agent and working environment
GitHub · capabilities and limitations of agents and code review

sections.title: Answer a question or create a ticket
paragraphs: In Agent Builder, give a helper one pretend handbook. Ask “Who reviews a missing badge request?” Check its cited line. If the next job is to file a request, explore Copilot Studio in an approved practice area. Make one test request and check its ticket number in the destination. Send the same practice request again. Decide what a repeat should do before using the helper with real work.
sources: Microsoft · Agent Builder and Copilot Studio compared
